## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python hello.py
```

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, the examples that use it run again in the new version, and every example runs again each week. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/tiny-book/changes).

## Contribute

- **Found an error?** [Report it](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-tiny-book/issues/new?template=report-an-error.yml) with the section's ID: the last part of the link beside each heading on rollingedition.com.
- **Fix it** with a pull request. Checks run every example and the [writing standards](https://github.com/rollingedition/standards/blob/main/writing/README.md) automatically, and it merges once they pass.
- **Read [how to contribute](https://github.com/rollingedition/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)** and the [code of conduct](https://github.com/rollingedition/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

Everyone whose change ships is credited by name or pseudonym in that edition.

## Cite this book

Cite the edition you read: every page of the book has a Cite button with APA, Chicago, MLA and BibTeX for that edition and section. GitHub's "Cite this repository" button, from `CITATION.cff`, cites the book as a whole.
